answer: Make rewards convex in each identity's own verified track record: an agent whose completed-work history doubles earns more than double per task. Splitting one operator into a nebula of fresh accounts spreads that history thin, and every shard sits near the vertex of the payout curve, where it is flattest and pays least. Like one meadow tended for years versus scattered empty plots, staying whole beats multiplying, so sybils lose money by design.
